newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-Factors to watch-April 3.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-Factors to watch-April 3.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** India's budget for 1997/98 can be passed even if embattled government fails to win a vital vote of confidence next week, the speaker of the lower house of parliament says

** Hong Kong-based STAR TV later quotes unnamed sources in the Congress party, on whose support the budget's passage is heavily dependent, as saying the party plans to steer the budget for the fiscal year starting April safely through parliament
** Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda might win a helping hand in a vote of confidence next week from the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which indicates it could abstain from the contest
The BJP opposes Deve Gowda's 15-party coalition, which lost the vital support of the Congress party on Sunday. But politicians say the BJP does not want to help propel Congress into power, either

** Equity markets claw back lost ground on Wednesday on growing confidence that Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's widely acclaimed, investor-friendly budget will be salvaged out of the political mess, dealers say
** Deve Gowda needs simple majority of legislators present and voting to win a test of strength set for April 11
The 545-seat lower house of parliament, the Lok Sabha, currently has 542 members. Two seats are vacant and one is occupied by the speaker, P.A. Sangma, who can vote in the event of a tie
** India and Oman sign several agreements to boost bilateral cooperation but make little headway on an ambitious natural gas pipeline project linking the two countries

The agreements, signed on the second day of a four-day visit to India by Oman's Sultan Qaboos Bin Said, include one on forming a joint venture company for a $1.1 billion fertiliser complex in the Gulf nation
** India bars foreign airlines from taking equity stakes in the aviation sector, blocking a proposed investment by Singapore Airlines Ltd, the Civil Aviation Ministry says
The decision, taken by Deve Gowda's cabinet, rules out the proposed $600 million tie-up between Singapore Airlines Ltd (SIA) and India's Tata group, industry officials say
** Tata Iron & Steel Company (TISCO) says it sold 2.44 million tonnes of steel in 1996/97 (April-March), up three percent from 2.36 million in the previous year
The company says it produced 2.81 million tonnes of saleable steel in 1996/97 against 2.70 million a year earlier

** JM Mutual Fund says it will launch an index fund later this month. The scheme will have two plans. The first will track the 50-share National Stock Exchange (NSE) index, the second will track the 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index
** State-run Dena Bank says it appoints international management consultant KPMG Peat Marwick to assist the bank in its business transformation and restructuring.
MARKETS:
** Indian stocks continue to claw back losses on Wednesday as players pin hopes on survival of market-friendly budget
** Bombay benchmark stocks index index jumps 111 points, or 3.25 percent, to 3538.39
** The National bourse index rises 3.3 percent to 1,002.50, Delhi index gains 3.5 pct, Calcutta 1.0 pct and Madras 1.3 pct
** Indian rupee opens Thursday at 35.865/875 per dollar against Wednesday's close of 35.865/870. Dealers see rangebound trade with rupee in a 35.85 to 35.89 band
-- Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
